purpose: Criterion c3 installed-runtime authentication semantics; evidence only, not current process identity or settlement authority.
runtimeFingerprintAlgorithm: SHA256(JSON.stringify(sorted recursive [relative file path,SHA256(bytes)] list)); symlinks refused. Full exact list is runtime-inventory.json inside archive.

verification.runtimeFilesReadFrom: Exact installed dist; full relevant files retained.
verification.functions: Exact contiguous complete bodies, no ellipses, rewriting, minification or removal of internal comments.
verification.sourceDerivationLimit: Runtime bytes are primary for the semantics audit. Source20cc is cross-reference; this preparation does not claim a new reproducible compiler build.

audit.claim: Fresh registration precedes real console and watches.
audit.finding: upCommand first reserves a temporary net-server probe. It then verifies operator login, calls registerRunnerIfIdle without a newToken or mutation override, retains answer.token in a local closure, closes the probe, starts the real console, and passes that token to each runWatchLoop. It does not recover a prior runner token from the database.

audit.claim: Registration is not mistaken for historical continuity.
audit.finding: Registration refuses a live runner or watch lease, mints32random bytes, stores only its SHA256, and writes registered_at inside the transaction. saveRunner sets registered_at later than both any old registration and historical reviewer start; default mutation has no replay key. The anchor demands unchanged credential hash/registration and an earlier saved reviewer incarnation, so replacement registration cannot satisfy those comparisons under the trusted-code model.

audit.claim: Every normal watch has a fresh closure-owned UUID.
audit.finding: The normal function unconditionally calls crypto.randomUUID(), authenticates lease acquisition for runner/token/repo/owner, and records that episode. The supplied flags do not choose incarnation. Its interval renews using that same closure token and UUID; failure latches leaseLost, aborts followers and stops admission. Cleanup releases only that owner.

audit.claim: Fresh watch heartbeat requires credential and exact unexpired lease owner together.
audit.evidence: heartbeatWatchLeaseAuthed, authenticate, getRunner, hashToken, sameDigest, transact, beginWriteWithin, heartbeatWatchLease
audit.finding: BEGIN IMMEDIATE encloses token-hash authentication and UPDATE. Authentication rejects unknown or retired runner and compares equal-length hashes with timingSafeEqual. UPDATE requires runner, repo, owner and expires_at>now; success requires changes>0. Only success touches runner heartbeat. A stale token, different UUID, expired lease or thrown write cannot count as a successful renewal.

audit.claim: Sealed implementation is necessary but not sufficient for a service anchor.
audit.finding: The anchor also requires current schema data ordering, fixed registration/credential/episode/generation, real advancement of watch heartbeat, exact managed process/listener arguments and stable untraced64-bit worker/supervisor identities. This package seals the code semantics on which those runtime checks rely; it supplies no live identity or exit observation.

limits: Conditional on ordinary trusted installed code, cryptographic randomness/credential secrecy and database integrity. A malicious privileged process that copies secrets, rewrites/restores code or edits rows is outside this established custody model.

This audit does not establish historical Codex source-coalition inheritance, historical environment/config completeness, absence of delegated jobs or surviving descendants, or permission to clear custody. The final recovery profile80bf and historical source/application/audit facts remain a separate evidence dependency; no additional recovery audit is included here.
All21 foundation source files/build inputs are unchanged from68bf. Prior native gate and criterion findings remain in checks.json; this correction is not independently verified.

validation.checksActuallyRun: Byte/range/hash/archive checks; node --check on each complete function, wrapped in a class only for Store method syntax. No runtime imports, database open, provider, census or test-suite rerun.
